brief: Who: coastal pantry + roast shop. Feel: calm host. Goal: rebrand that reads craft without trend. Pillars: warmth, honesty, unhurried retail.
voice: Two counters, one oven, and a queue that starts before we open. We bake what the day needs and stop when it is gone.
logoDirection: Harbor arc + hearth circle (mark) with Fraunces wordmark. Horizontal primary; mark alone for stamps and stickers. No drop shadows.
logoClearspace: Clearspace ~ half the mark height on all sides. Prefer full-color on cream; reverse on deep green covers.

detective.goal: Look like a neighborhood staple, not a trend cafe — so locals and visitors both trust the shelves and the pour.
detective.story: Started as a weekend farmers-market table; three years later we roast small-batch and stock pantry goods from coastal makers.
detective.usp: Small-batch coffee and coastal pantry goods with a calm, host-at-home retail experience.
detective.audience: Adults 28–55 who cook at home, gift thoughtfully, and prefer quiet shops over loud chains.
detective.feel: Welcomed, steady, a little proud of what they picked up.
detective.audiencePains: Confused shelves, Instagram-only brands, coffee that tastes like marketing.
detective.competitors: Local chain cafes; glossy gift-shop brands; big-box “artisan” lines.
detective.brandAsPerson: A generous neighbor who always has a spare mug and never oversells.
detective.inspirationLinks: Quiet retail interiors, linen paper, linen, morning window light, ceramic cups.
detective.avoid: Neon, faux-distress, clipart coffee beans, loud hustle slogans.
detective.deliverables: Shelf talkers, thank-you card, tote mark.
detective.technical: AI/PDF for print, PNG/SVG for web and POS.
detective.existingAssets: Keep the wooden spoon illustration from year one (redrawn cleaner). Drop the old teal gradient.

feedbackNotes: Stakeholder review: hierarchy on bags is clear. Keep wordmark quieter than mark on small stamps. Feels like home without cottage cliché.
handoffNote: Ship: logo lockups, roles (cover/text/accent/quiet), type pair, messaging pillars, imagery rules, business card specimen, brand-book PDF + tokens.
learnings: What worked: cream field + deep green. Felt honest: retiring the teal gradient. Next: more real shelf photography.

discoveryAnswers.story: Harbor & Hearth began as a market table selling small-batch coffee and pantry goods from coastal makers. The name is about home (hearth) and the harbor town that supplies the goods.
discoveryAnswers.offering: Small-batch roasted coffee, pantry staples, and a calm neighborhood retail shop with a short pour menu.
discoveryAnswers.problem: The old identity felt like a trendy pop-up. Regulars still came, but visitors could not tell if we were serious about craft or just cute packaging.
discoveryAnswers.usp: Coastal pantry + roast quality with host-at-home hospitality — never loud, never disposable.
discoveryAnswers.fiveYearVision: Two shops, a tight wholesale line for cafes that share our pace, and a brand book that staff can use without a designer on call.
discoveryAnswers.targetAudience: Home cooks and gift-givers 28–55 in coastal towns and nearby cities; design-aware but allergy to hype.
discoveryAnswers.audiencePains: Hard-to-read labels, brands that feel like ads, coffee that overpromises.
discoveryAnswers.desiredFeeling: Calm confidence — “I can take this home and it will fit.”
discoveryAnswers.competitors: Regional cafe chains (too loud); lifestyle gift brands (too glossy); commodity grocery “artisan” (too cheap).
discoveryAnswers.brandAsPerson: Warm neighbor, soft voice, never showy.
discoveryAnswers.visualStyleKeywords: Linen, timber, cream paper, deep green, soft gold
discoveryAnswers.inspirationLinks: Quiet Scandinavian grocery, Japanese stationery packaging, coastal pottery studios.
discoveryAnswers.admiredBrands: Aesop (restraint), Blue Bottle early packaging (clarity), local ceramic studios (hand feel).
discoveryAnswers.elementsToAvoid: Neon gradients, faux chalkboard, stock bean photos, aggressive FOMO language.
discoveryAnswers.mustHaveDeliverables: Logo system, palette, type, guidelines PDF, business cards, bag/label system.
discoveryAnswers.existingAssets: Wooden spoon mark (keep idea), customer photo library of shop windows, old teal #2A9D8F (retire).
discoveryAnswers.fileFormats: AI, PDF, PNG, SVG, brand-book PDF
